clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old man presented with episodic headaches, palpitations, sweating, anxiety, and elevated blood pressure. Biochemical testing showed elevated plasma catecholamines and metanephrines confirming catecholamine excess. Imaging (CT and MRI) localized a 3 cm left adrenal mass with local invasion. Histopathological examination post-surgery confirmed pheochromocytoma, demonstrating capsular and vascular invasion with low mitotic rate and Ki-67 index of 5%. Brain MRI was normal, ruling out other causes of symptoms.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Elevated plasma catecholamines and metanephrines consistent with catecholamine excess
Imaging showed 3 cm left adrenal mass with local tissue invasion
Histopathological confirmation of pheochromocytoma with capsular and vascular invasion
Normal brain MRI excluding alternative neurological etiologies

remaining_uncertainties: Lack of documented surgical treatment details
No information on postoperative clinical course, patient outcome, or follow-up
